headline: Scalable tools and foundation models reshape molecular evolution inference
label: Computational Tools For Molecular Evolution
summary: Protein foundation models, GPU covariance-model search and orthology benchmarks are changing how evolutionary inference is scaled and validated.
synthesis: The dominant thread is tooling that either accelerates evolutionary inference or tests it against known truth. Infernal-GPU parallelizes covariance-model dynamic programming on GPUs, recalibrating Rfam E-values and recovering remote structured-RNA homologs. OrthoSimulator instead generates empirically calibrated simulated datasets with known orthogroups and gene trees so orthology inference can be benchmarked against ground truth. The protein foundation model review covers alignment-free evolutionary analyses, while the AlphaFold study shows where predictions diverge from biologically relevant structural states for non-globular proteins, a reminder that model outputs require validation. MolEvolvR packages domain-centric searches, phylogenies and domain architecture into a web app for protein evolution. What is new is the pairing of computational acceleration with explicit ground-truth testing. These items differ in task and method, so this emphasis is dominant rather than shared by all.
